items.text: A "Back" button at the top of the new-block pop-up (also in the Text and Image pop-ups) returns to the list of block kinds. Effect: a wrong pick no longer means closing the pop-up and opening "Add block" again. Asked for after using the editor.

A card at the top of the dashboard tells members who still have a WhatsApp rotator block that the block is being retired. It can be hidden for a week, and it names the end date only once one is decided. Reason: owners need to know before the block goes away.

The nine cards are grouped into four sections (Search & sharing, Privacy, Tools, Versions), and the search-engine preview sits next to the title and description on wide screens. A refused setting opens the section it belongs to. Reason: one long list of cards was hard to scan.

The pop-up is split into short sections (Content, Look, Schedule, Advanced). A section with nothing in it for that kind of block is not shown, and a divider or spacer has none. If saving is refused, the section that needs attention opens. Reason: one long form was hard to read, especially for links.

There is one "Music" block for Spotify, SoundCloud, Apple Music and YouTube Music links, instead of separate Spotify and SoundCloud blocks, and the app store link, RSS feed and poll blocks are no longer offered. Pages that already have these blocks keep them and can still edit them. Reason: the picker was long and several kinds overlapped.
No new rotator block can be made; blocks already on a page keep working and can be edited. Use a normal link block or a LinkHop link instead.
The position choice is one row of two buttons, and each social icon is one short row. Effect: the list is shorter and easier to arrange.
A panel with little in it keeps a readable width on wide screens instead of stretching into an empty card, and the Footer section is gone (see the public pages item below).
The picture shape choice is hidden, with a short note, for the Hero and Cutout headers, which do not use it. Your choice is kept if you switch back.
"Part of Hop Easy Link" moved to the bottom left of the sidebar. Reason: under the page content it landed in an odd place on long pages such as the editor.

For a signed-in member, the Back links on the information pages and the report page, the BioHop logo and the Dashboard button now lead to the BioHop dashboard instead of the home page or the HOP ID dashboard. Visitors who are not signed in still go to the home page.
The "Powered by BioHop" line is always shown, and the editor preview says the same. The switch for hiding it is gone, so pages that had hidden it show it again.

items.where: Editor, dragging blocks in two tabs
items.text: When the page was changed in another tab, saving the new block order is now refused with a clear message in your language, instead of quietly replacing the other tab's changes. The editor now sends the page version it knows, which the server has been able to check since version 1.3.2.
The language list in the header no longer runs off the right edge of a phone screen.

entries.title: Safer saving of the block order

items.text: Saving the order of your blocks is stricter on the server. It answers the same for a block that belongs to someone else and for one that does not exist, so block numbers of other pages cannot be guessed; it refuses a list that is too long, repeats a block, or carries a position outside the page's block limit; it saves the whole new order in one step or not at all; and it is rate-limited like the other editor actions. Nothing the editor sends is refused by this.
Blocks that share the same position are always listed in the same order, in the editor, on the public page and in the API. Reason: before, the database could choose a different order each time.

When a request to save the order carries the page version it was made from, it is refused with "changed in another tab" if the page changed meanwhile, like saving the other fields. The editor sends it from version 1.4.0 on.
An empty entry in the social icons list is refused on save and ignored when the page is read, so older data with an empty entry can no longer stop the editor from opening.

Dragging a block now moves the block you drag. Before, a drag could move another block, or add an empty "Untitled" block after which no drag and no save worked until a reload. The new order is read from the blocks themselves after the drop, an error can no longer freeze dragging, the dragged block looks like a block, and a drag made while the order is being saved is saved too. The social icons list works the same way. Orders scrambled earlier are not repaired automatically; Settings > Versions can bring back an earlier one.

A block that was just added can be dragged at once, and the preview follows a drag. A move the list cannot apply refreshes the list and says so instead of staying silent; pressing Restore twice restores once; Archive removes the block you archived even if you dragged another one meanwhile.

items.where: Public pages with a warning or password
items.text: A page with an age or content warning, or a password, opens after one confirmation and stays on the address the visitor came by. Before, the first confirmation was lost and the visitor ended up on the app's own address. The source of a QR or NFC visit is kept.
The QR logo in the Profile tab uploads (it always failed before), and the next save after it is no longer refused as "changed in another tab".
Uploads of the cover, background, share picture, favicon and images say why a file was refused instead of "Failed to upload".
Text typed in "Select existing link", the Add block search and the page password field no longer runs over the search icon.
The hero header fills the width of the page and of the editor preview instead of sitting to the left.
Upload buttons offer the file types they take: SVG only for custom block icons and the QR logo. Choosing an SVG somewhere else says so at once, in nine languages.
The theme and the language are now shared with the other HOP apps, so a choice made in one app is the choice in the others. Public bio pages keep their own theme.

The home and information pages name one address per language, list the nine languages, share a picture preview, and the home page describes BioHop as a web application. Signed-in screens ask search engines to stay away. Reason: so each language of a page is found in search.

items.where: Editor and public pages, "Receive payment" block
items.text: The page owner picks a payment method (PayPal.me, Cash App, Venmo, Solana Pay, UPI, EPC SEPA, PromptPay or VietQR), fills in its fields, and can set a fixed amount, let visitors type one, and add a note. The public page shows the payee, method, details and amount as text and draws the QR code in the visitor's browser; nothing is sent anywhere. Reason: owners asked for a simple way to get paid.

On an iPhone, iPad or Android phone, a block that points to a well-known app (YouTube, WhatsApp, Telegram, TikTok and others) opens the app. On an iPhone without the app, the visitor is taken to the web address after a moment. Reason: links to apps used to open in the browser.

A payment block now refuses account details that do not have the right shape for their method, also when the request does not come from the editor. Saving other settings of a payment block keeps its stored payment details.
PayHop (pay.hel.ink) joins the family and is named in the FAQ, the home page and the official page in nine languages. "payhop" and "pay" cannot be used as page addresses.
When you switch accounts at HOP ID, the old account no longer stays signed in here: the home page, the information pages and every signed-in page confirm with HOP ID every few minutes.
The page can show a history built when the app is updated. Shared links to the information pages now show a preview picture and title.

The boxes are laid out by the shared family grid, the "Part of the HOP family" section and the BioHop logo (a small pixel page with three lines) are updated, and the family tiles sit in one calm row on wide screens.

Every app shows "Part of Hop Easy Link" as the first row of its footer, the footer no longer has a language row (the language menu in the top bar is the one place), and signing out brings you back to BioHop through HOP ID.

The "Save contact" file can no longer be tampered with through a name, number, e-mail or company containing special characters. Reason: before, a line break in a name could add extra fields to the file.
The form is translated in all nine languages.
"filehop" cannot be used as a page address, like the names of the other HOP apps.
The page lists every release again; it had been left out of date.
FileHop (file.hel.ink) is named wherever BioHop lists its sibling apps, in all nine languages, and "filehop" cannot be used as a page address.
A link block can point to one of your public notes (off by default). Reason: owners wanted to share a note on their page.
A picture already uploaded to PixelHop can be picked for the image block, the carousel, the avatar, the cover and the favicon (off by default).
Plain public pages can be served from the edge of the network to be faster, only for pages without a password, warning, form or poll, and only for visitors without a session.

items.where: Behind the scenes, picture and note pickers
items.text: The calls to PixelHop and NoteHop can be signed with a secret of their own, so a leak on one of those servers can no longer be used to sign in here.
Links to a known phishing kit are recognised and refused, and the shared list of blocked domains is updated.
Links to encrypted NoteHop notes are refused everywhere a page or block is saved, not only in address fields.
The list now shows your short links; it was always empty, and each search left one more access token behind. When LinkHop cannot be reached, it says so instead of "No links found".
The link picker and the link library are translated into the nine languages, their buttons work with the keyboard, and the spinner stands still with reduced motion.
A draft no longer links to its public address or QR code, which showed an error page.
Uploading a picture that is too large now says so instead of failing with an error.
Inputs, selects and buttons share one radius and one height, and controls are 44 pixels tall on touch screens and narrow windows.

BioHop, the link-in-bio app of the HOP family, is split out of LinkHop: public pages at hel.ink/b/your-name, an editor at bio.hel.ink, themes, uploads and analytics. People sign in with HOP ID; there are no separate accounts.

Many block kinds: links, shop products with variants and stock, collections, sign-up forms with entries you can download, polls, feeds, embeds, audio, PDF, picture carousel, status chip and floating button. Blocks can be scheduled, given a PIN, archived, and sent elsewhere by country, device or time of day.
"New bio page" is a short guided setup with a live phone, and a public Linktree page can be imported as a draft.
The editor saves by itself about a second after you stop typing and keeps versions you can restore.
A greeting, clicks this week against last week, a setup checklist, analytics by page, link and source (QR code, NFC tag, installed web app), and a command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K).

Content warnings (sensitive and adult), four header layouts, themes, wallpaper and a share picture. Privacy by default: no outside fonts or scripts, visitor addresses kept only as a coded value for 30 days, and trackers only after consent.
The interface, the READMEs and the documentation site are in nine languages: English, Chinese, German, Indonesian, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish, French and Russian.
A one-command installer, updater and uninstaller for self-hosting.
The editor is one page that scrolls normally with the preview beside it; on phones the preview opens as a full-screen sheet. Reason: the old fixed-height box was cramped.
Public pages load their own small files, pictures are shrunk when uploaded, and a first-time reader of a plain page gets no session and no cookies.
The admin pages moved to the HOP control panel (Imperium).
Pictures, icons, audio, PDFs and slides on a public page load again; they live on the app address while the page is on hel.ink.
Uploaded background pictures, SVG icons, QR logos and thumbnails now save, and a block's custom icon is kept.
Saving the search section no longer fails when an older, longer title is stored.
The preview scrolls on every browser and on touch.
A link to hel.ink or another HOP app is kept as typed instead of being wrapped in a short link.
Signing out at HOP ID now ends the session here too, even when BioHop was down at that moment, and a deleted account has its sessions and files removed.
Links to encrypted NoteHop notes are refused, and a suspended member is sent to the notice at HOP ID.
The feed reader and the webhook sender connect only to addresses that were checked.
Fonts, icons and scripts are no longer loaded from outside hosts; everything ships with the app.
